rows.name: The Broken Robot Artist
steps: Educator plays 'The Broken Robot Artist' at the whiteboard: the class must make the robot draw a perfect square.
When a child says 'Draw a line', draw a messy squiggle; explain the instruction was too vague.
When a child says 'Draw a straight line across', draw it off the board; explain the robot was not told when to stop.
A child gives an exact command such as '30 centimeters to the right, then stop'; draw it.
Say 'Turn' spins the robot all the way round; the class asks for a 90-degree turn.
Restate: computers cannot guess what you mean.

levels.0: Board shows only squiggles; no instruction names a length or a turn.
levels.1: Instructions name a length but skip the 90-degree turn, so a corner is missing.
levels.2: Four equal sides with four 90-degree turns are named, and the board square closes.
levels.3: Instructions are shortened after a trial run, with a reason for each cut.

rows.name: Play acting
steps: Read 'बल्लू हाथी का बालस्वर' aloud as a play.
Discuss the story (चर्चा).
Assign parts and rehearse.
Act the scene with clear voices (अभिनय).
Draw the set (दृश्यावली-निर्माण) for a scene.

levels.1: Lines are said without expression.
levels.2: Character from 'बल्लू हाथी का बालस्वर' is acted with a clear voice.
levels.3: Set drawing (दृश्यावली) is made for a scene.

rows.name: Learning notice board
steps: Recall the lessons of the term in a circle (चर्चा).
Make a notice board (सूचना बोर्ड) for the class.
Add drawings (चित्र-निर्माण) with captions.
Arrange the information in order. (suggested)
Present one item aloud. (suggested)

levels.0: Board has no drawing or caption from the term's lessons.
levels.1: Drawings are added but captions are written or ordered with the educator's help.
levels.2: Notice board shows drawings with the child's own captions, arranged in the order the lessons came.
levels.3: Why one lesson comes before another, and what it led to, is explained aloud.

rows.name: Letter about a visit
steps: Read 'एक दिन लाल किले में' (पत्र) aloud.
Discuss what the writer saw.
Write a letter (पत्र-लेखन) about a place visited.
Add the opposite meaning words with 'नहीं'.
Share the letter with a partner.

levels.0: Letter on the Red Fort visit is blank.
levels.1: Letter lacks the visit details.
levels.2: Letter in the letter format describes a place visited.
levels.3: Letter adds a bio-data style line about the writer.

rows.name: Daily journal
steps: Suggested: Open the journal.
Suggested: Write about something that happened in school today, such as a lesson or an object seen.
Suggested: Leave out feelings and anything from home.
Suggested: Re-read the entry.
Suggested: Share one line if the pupil chooses.

Suggested: Discuss its meaning.
Suggested: Each child uses it in a sentence.
Suggested: Share sentences.

levels.2: Word of the day sits correctly in a sentence of the pupil's own.
levels.3: Word is used in two different ways.

Suggested: Practise in pairs.
Suggested: Spell aloud.
Suggested: Score together.

levels.0: Words are misspelled in every attempt.

levels.2: Whole weekly list is spelled correctly aloud.

Suggested: Solve with the clues.
Suggested: Find hidden words.

levels.1: A few clues are answered with wrong spellings.
levels.2: Crossword is filled from the clues and hidden words are found.

Suggested: Add details to expand it.
Suggested: Write a dialogue between two characters.
Suggested: Read aloud.

rows.name: Mental maths within the time
steps: Suggested: Call out mental maths questions.
Suggested: Solve with a stated strategy.
Suggested: Give the answer within the time

levels.1: Answer given after the time or by counting on fingers.
levels.2: Answer right within the time given.
levels.3: Strategy used (for example doubling, near ten) is said aloud.

rows.name: Mini science observation
steps: Suggested: Choose one thing at home that changes, such as a seed on wet cotton.
Suggested: Each day draw it and write the date and one change seen.
Suggested: After two weeks bring the record to class and tell one change.

levels.1: One dated observation, or several undated ones.
levels.2: Dated observations over the fortnight show the changes seen.
levels.3: What caused one change and what would happen next is said.

rows.name: Memory drawing and doodle
steps: Suggested: Show an object for 30 seconds.
Suggested: Cover it.
Suggested: Draw from memory.
Suggested: Write sentences about the doodle.

levels.0: Drawing bears no link to the object.
levels.1: Drawing misses key details.
levels.2: Drawing from memory shows the main features of the object, and sentences describe a doodle.
levels.3: Extra details are added from a second look.

Unit bullets: Builds observation skills, memory, and attention to detail; Encourages creativity, observation, and descriptive writing skills. [audit] Also named in Routines!B15 (Routines B15: Doodle & Describe, home, November, once a fortnight; memory drawing is in the timetable.). Steps stay suggested; basis unchanged.

rows.name: Line maze challenge
steps: Warm-up sketch activity with pencils on A4.
Introduce types of lines (wavy, zigzag, dotted, thick, thin) with board drawings or slides.
Line maze challenge: each pupil draws a path using 4 or more types of line.
Display on the wall as 'Our Line Worlds'.
rows.materials: Chart of line types, sharpened pencils, black markers, A4 paper.

levels.0: Maze path has fewer than two kinds of line.
levels.1: Maze path uses two or three kinds of line and one is shaky.
levels.2: Maze path uses four or more kinds of line, thick and thin, straight and curved.
levels.3: Wavy, zigzag and dotted lines are named aloud as the path is traced.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Shape scavenger hunt and Shape Creature
steps: Shape scavenger hunt in the classroom, looking at objects.
Cut shapes from coloured paper.
Make a collage by arranging the cut-outs into an abstract 'Shape Creature'.
Show one Kandinsky image as background.
Display on the Shape Creatures Jungle board.
rows.materials: Magazines, child-safe scissors, glue, coloured paper.

levels.0: Creature uses only one kind of shape.
levels.1: Creature mixes shapes but none is organic.
levels.2: Creature mixes geometric and organic shapes, each pointed out.
levels.3: Creature's shapes are sorted aloud into geometric and organic groups.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Pattern Play on grid paper
steps: Create repeating patterns on grid paper.
Use colour to enhance the rhythm of the pattern.
Add each pupil's square to the class pattern mural (collaborative).
Display as 'Our Class Quilt'.

levels.1: A repeat starts but breaks by the third unit.
levels.2: Pattern repeats cleanly across the whole grid row.
levels.3: Second row varies the colour rhythm while keeping the repeat.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Pattern in Culture: Warli and African prints
steps: Show simple Indian (Warli) and African (Ndebele) patterns.
Children replicate one on brown paper using white paint or crayons.
Educator explains symmetry and motifs.
Display on the Cultural Patterns Wall.
rows.materials: Brown paper, white paint or crayons, pattern pictures.

levels.0: Copy has no motif from the model.
levels.1: One motif is copied and its origin is not named.
levels.2: Warli or Ndebele motifs are copied and the place they come from is named.
levels.3: A motif's repeat or symmetry is pointed out on the copy.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Drawing with Pattern: animal silhouettes
steps: Draw animal silhouettes.
Fill the inside with different pattern zones.
Add a background in crayon resist (watercolour wash).
Display as 'Pattern Zoo'.

levels.1: Silhouette has one pattern throughout.
levels.2: Silhouette has different line, shape and pattern zones.
levels.3: Wash background keeps the crayon patterns showing through.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Artist Week: Klee cityscape or Kusama dots
steps: View and discuss selected art by Paul Klee or Yayoi Kusama.
Make a Klee-inspired cityscape or Kusama-style polka-dot art.
Ask questions about the art and its style.
Display in the 'Inspired By…' corner.
rows.materials: Prints of the artists' work, paper, paints.

levels.0: Artist's lines or patterns are not mentioned.
levels.1: One line or pattern from the artist is noted.
levels.2: Lines and patterns used by Klee or Kusama are named from the print.
levels.3: Own artwork shows the same lines or dots, and a likeness is pointed out.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Colour wheel on a paper plate
steps: Mix red, yellow and blue to create the secondary colours.
Make a simple colour wheel on a paper plate.
Hang the wheels as the display.
rows.materials: Paper plates, red, yellow and blue paint, brushes.

levels.0: Plate has only the three primaries.
levels.1: Plate has one secondary, mixed with help.
levels.2: Plate shows orange, green and purple mixed from the primaries.
levels.3: Mixing recipe is told aloud for each secondary.

rows.note: Educator reflection in source ('who mixes confidently, who hesitates') is an observation prompt, not recorded here. From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Warm and cool colour art
steps: Discuss the sun and ice as metaphors for warm and cool.
Create abstract art using warm or cool tones.
Title the art with a mood-word from the word chart, e.g. 'Fiery Night', 'Cool Breeze'.
Display as a gallery by colour tone.
rows.materials: Paint trays, brushes, mood word chart.

levels.0: Painting mixes warm and cool colours at random.
levels.1: Painting is mostly warm or cool with a stray colour.
levels.2: Painting stays in warm or cool tones and the group is named.
levels.3: Title from the mood word chart suits the tones chosen.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Mood Monsters
steps: Suggested: Pick a mood word card (children do not write about their own feelings).
Suggested: Create a monster using shapes and colours that match the mood.
Suggested: Show on the 'Mood Monsters Parade'.
rows.materials: Mood word cards, paper, paints or collage materials.
rows.note: Named in G2-G3 Visual Arts Curriculum (Week 9: Mood Monsters); steps are built from the name, not taken from the doc text. Source says 'children choose an emotion'; reworded so no child's own feelings are recorded. From the school's own curriculum document. Self-expression/self-reflection activity: no graded levels (ADR 0037); look_fors only; no feelings or reflections recorded.
look_fors: Takes a mood word card without asking others which to take.
Uses at least two colours on the monster that suit the card's mood word.
Shows the monster to a partner when asked.

rows.name: Starry Night sky
steps: Study Starry Night.
Create a layered sky using oil pastels and tissue collage.
Discuss what the painting shows through colour and brush strokes.
Display as 'Our Starry Skies'.
rows.materials: Oil pastels, tissue paper, print of Starry Night.

levels.0: Sky has flat colour with no stroke marks.
levels.1: Strokes appear in one part of the sky.
levels.2: Swirling strokes in layered colours cover the sky.
levels.3: Stroke and colour choices are linked to movement in the painting.

source.cell: Week 10–11: Famous Artist Focus – Van Gogh’s Starry Night

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Colour reflection and gallery walk
steps: Walk around the class display with reflection sheets.
Hold a peer discussion on a favourite artwork.
Use art words (colour, line) in the talk.

levels.1: Artwork is named but not described.
levels.2: Artwork is described using words such as colour and line.
levels.3: Process of making is described along with the look of the work.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Touch and texture rubbings
steps: Sensory exploration: pass around textured objects (bark, foil, sandpaper).
Make texture rubbings using crayons.
Discuss which textures felt soft, rough or smooth.
Display as the Texture Explorers chart.

levels.1: Rubbings are clear but textures are not named.
levels.2: Each rubbing is labelled rough, smooth, soft or hard.
levels.3: Real texture is told from picture texture on two samples.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Texture collage landscape
steps: Collect scrap materials (fabric, thread, foil, leaves).
Design a landscape or imaginary scene using the textures.
Glue and display as 'Tactile Landscapes'.
rows.materials: Scrap fabric, thread, foil, leaves, glue.

levels.1: Two textures are glued without a plan.
levels.2: Landscape uses several textures to show land, sky and water.
levels.3: Each texture used is named by touch.

rows.note: Source says to ask children to bring bits from home; school supplies are used instead. From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Visual texture drawing
steps: Observe texture photos (fur, woodgrain, pebbles).
Create black-and-white texture swatches using pencil lines and shading.
Display as the 'Texture Tiles' wall.

levels.1: Swatch shows one texture with lines only.
levels.2: Swatches imitate fur, woodgrain and pebbles with lines and shading.
levels.3: Photo and swatch are matched by texture word.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Rousseau jungle with layered texture
steps: Study Henri Rousseau's work.
Paint the background.
Layer textured leaves and animals.
Join into the 'Jungle Wall' group mural.
rows.materials: Paint, textured paper and fabric, glue.

levels.1: Leaves are added but not layered.
levels.2: Background paint plus layered textured leaves and animals.
levels.3: Real and drawn textures are told apart in the mural.

source.tab: Week 16–17: Artist Focus – Henri Rousseau Jungle
source.cell: Week 16–17: Artist Focus – Henri Rousseau Jungle

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Paper sculpture 3D creatures
steps: Learn folding, curling and stacking.
Make 3D creatures from paper strips and forms.
Introduce tabs, slots and bridges for joining.
Display as the '3D Zoo' on tables.

levels.1: Form stands but is joined only by glue.
levels.2: Folded, curled and stacked creature stands on its own.
levels.3: Tabs and slots join the parts and the technique is named.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Clay or dough: pinch, roll, press, coil
steps: Explore pinch, roll, press and coil techniques.
Make pinch pots or story plates.
If festive, make an eco-friendly diya, animal or character.
Display as the 'Mini Museum'.

levels.1: One shape is made by pressing only.
levels.2: Pot or plate shows pinch and coil work with even walls.
levels.3: Technique used on each part is named.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Junk sculpture: robots and fantasy machines
steps: Create robots or fantasy machines from recyclable materials.
Work in groups.
Show at the 'Future Machines Expo'.
rows.materials: Recycled boxes, bottle caps, tape, glue.

levels.1: Machine is joined but falls over.
levels.2: Machine stands, built from recycled materials in a group.
levels.3: Machine's parts are named and the reused material is told.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Japanese fish kites (Koinobori)
steps: Learn about Japanese Children's Day and its symbolism.
Use paper rolls or kite shapes.
Decorate with patterns and hang from string.
Display as 'Flying Fish Lane'.
rows.materials: Paper rolls or kite shapes, string, paints.

levels.1: Kite has a pattern that is not repeated.
levels.2: Kite is patterned with repeats and hangs on string.
levels.3: Japanese Children's Day is linked to the fish shape.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: African masks
steps: Show simple African mask examples.
Design a face with bold shapes and colours.
Optional: mount on sticks.
Display as 'Faces from Afar'.

levels.1: Mask has bold colour but one shape.
levels.2: Mask has bold shapes and colours that suit a mood word.
levels.3: Mask is symmetrical and its choices are explained.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Aboriginal dot art
steps: Learn the symbolism and dot technique.
Create an animal or path story with cotton bud dots.
Display as 'Animal Journeys'.

levels.0: Dots are scattered with no shape.
levels.1: Dots form an outline only.
levels.2: Dots form an animal or a path.
levels.3: Story told by the picture is described.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Mexican papel picado
steps: Fold tissue paper for symmetry.
Cut shapes out of the folded paper.
Open and hang as 'Festival of Flags'.

levels.1: Design is cut but one side differs.
levels.2: Opened flag is symmetrical across the fold.
levels.3: Fold lines and the mirror image are pointed out.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Scandinavian weaving on card looms
steps: Learn basic over-under weaving.
Use paper strips or yarn on card looms.
Display as 'Woven Wonders'.
rows.materials: Card looms, paper strips or yarn.

levels.1: Weave goes over-under for a few rows.
levels.2: Rows go over-under all the way across the loom.
levels.3: A pattern or colour sequence is set in the weave.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Art around the world pin map
steps: Suggested: Pin each pupil's work near the country studied on a world map.
Suggested: Say what the art is and where it comes from.
Suggested: Compare two pinned crafts: say what is alike and what is different.

levels.0: Work is pinned with no place named.
levels.1: Place is named but not the craft.
levels.2: Craft and country are matched on the map.
levels.3: Two crafts are compared for pattern and material.

rows.name: Portfolio building
steps: Organise works into folders.
Choose 3 pieces to keep in the portfolio.
Fill in a mini reflection sheet: Why do I like this? What I learned?
rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document. Self-expression/self-reflection activity: no graded levels (ADR 0037); look_fors only; no feelings or reflections recorded.
look_fors: Sorts the folder into piles before choosing pieces.
Fills in the reflection sheet for each chosen piece.
Places the chosen pieces in the portfolio folder without a reminder.

rows.name: Final artwork project
steps: Choose a theme and a medium (drawing, collage, sculpture).
Plan, draft and make the final piece.
Display as 'Our Masterpieces'.

levels.1: Draft exists but the final piece differs without reason.
levels.2: Plan, draft and final piece match the chosen theme.
levels.3: A skill from the year is named in the finished piece.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Exhibition setup and art exhibition
steps: Mount and label the work.
Write a guided artist bio.
Set up tables, boards and name tags.
On the day, take visitors around the gallery.

levels.0: Work is hung with no title card.
levels.1: Title card is written with the educator's help.
levels.2: Work is mounted with its own title card and a visitor's question is answered in a sentence.
levels.3: Answer to a visitor points to a part of the piece and says how it was made.

source.cell: Week 35–36: Exhibition Setup / Art Exhibition + Certificates

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: 3D name stand
steps: Fold chart into a standing shape.
Write and decorate names.
Add designs and patterns.

levels.1: Stand folds but the name is hard to read.
levels.2: Standing chart shows the name clearly with patterns.
levels.3: Folds measured with a scale come out even.

rows.note: Source reference to names kept: pupil's own name on own work only. From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Nature texture rubbing
steps: Place a leaf below the paper.
Rub a crayon gently.
Observe the texture impressions.

levels.1: Leaf outline shows but no texture.
levels.2: Vein and bark texture show through the rubbing.
levels.3: Textures from two sources are compared aloud.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

rows.name: Animal clay sculptures
steps: Educator demonstrates joining clay parts.
Create animals.
Add details and textures.
